title: Opening hours and errands ({ouvrir}, {fermer}, {passer}, {oublier})
description: Say when a place opens and closes, that you will drop by, and what someone forgot: {La boulangerie ouvre à sept heures.} {Je passe chez toi ce soir.}
can_do: Say when a place opens and closes: {La boulangerie ouvre à sept heures.}
Say that you will drop by: {Je passe chez toi ce soir.}
Say what someone forgot: {J'ai oublié ma clé.}

vocabulary.gloss: to drop by; to pass; to spend (time)
vocabulary.note: {passer chez quelqu'un} is to drop by their place. In the past, dropping by takes {être} ({je suis passée chez toi}) and spending time takes {avoir} ({j'ai passé le week-end ici}).
vocabulary.example_fr: Je passe chez toi ce soir.
vocabulary.example_en: I'll drop by your place tonight.

vocabulary.note: {oublier de} + a verb is to forget to do something: {n'oublie pas de passer}.
An -ir verb with the present endings of {parler}: {j'ouvre}, {nous ouvrons}. Its past participle is {ouvert}.
vocabulary.example_fr: La boulangerie ouvre à sept heures.

vocabulary.note: A regular -er verb. On a door, {fermé} means closed.
vocabulary.example_fr: La boulangerie ferme à vingt heures.
vocabulary.example_en: The bakery closes at eight in the evening.

vocabulary.note: Spoken: it ends a story and gets to the point.
vocabulary.example_fr: J'ai oublié ma clé, maman travaille ce soir. Bref, je peux pas entrer.
vocabulary.example_en: I forgot my key, Mum is working tonight. Anyway, I can't get in.

vocabulary.note: Spoken {oui} between friends. To a teacher or a shopkeeper, say {oui}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Tu passes chez moi ce soir ? Ouais, à huit heures.
vocabulary.example_en: Are you dropping by tonight? Yeah, at eight.

concepts.definition: At the start of a sentence, {bref} sums up what came before and gives the main point. It is common in speech.
concepts.example: {J'ai oublié ma clé, maman travaille ce soir. Bref, je peux pas entrer.} (I forgot my key, Mum is working tonight. Anyway, I can't get in.)

phrases.fr: Je passe chez ma voisine ce soir.
Mon copain a oublié sa clé.

items.situation: Maya reads the sign on the door of Karim's bakery: {Ouvert de sept heures à vingt heures}. Noé asks her what time it opens. Answer as Maya: it opens at seven.
accept: la boulangerie ouvre à sept heures

mistakes.feedback: {ouvert} is the past participle. In the present: {elle ouvre}.

items.text: Noé : Euh, et elle ___ à quelle heure ? Maya : À vingt heures.
items.gloss: Noé: Um, and what time does it close? Maya: At eight in the evening.

mistakes.feedback: {elle} is the bakery, so no -s: {elle ferme}.
Noé knows when it opens now. He asks when it closes: {ferme}.

items.text: Le monsieur qui ___ la boulangerie à sept heures, c'est Karim.
items.gloss: The man who opens the bakery at seven is Karim.

mistakes.feedback: One man, so {il ouvre}: {le monsieur qui ouvre}.

items.instruction: It is hot in Léa's flat, and Léa and Noé open the window together. Start the sentence with {nous}.
items.shown: Il fait chaud et humide, j'ouvre la fenêtre.
items.answer: il fait chaud et humide, nous ouvrons la fenêtre
accept: il fait chaud et humide nous ouvrons la fenêtre

mistakes.answer: il fait chaud et humide, nous ouvrez la fenêtre
il fait chaud et humide, nous ouvre la fenêtre

items.text: Noé : ___ la fenêtre, il y a une abeille ! Léa : Mais non, c'est un papillon.
items.gloss: Noé: Close the window, there's a bee! Léa: No, it's a butterfly.

mistakes.feedback: A command to {tu} drops the -s of an -er verb: {Ferme}.
The window is already open. Noé wants it closed: {Ferme}.

items.text: Le samedi, la bibliothèque et la piscine ___ à neuf heures.
items.gloss: On Saturdays, the library and the pool open at nine.

items.instruction: Maya reaches the library at nine in the evening. Say the opposite of what she hoped.
items.shown: La bibliothèque où Léa travaille est ouverte.
items.answer: la bibliothèque où léa travaille est fermée

mistakes.answer: la bibliothèque où léa travaille est fermé
la bibliothèque où léa travaille est ferme

items.question: Noé tells Léa: {Hugo est passé chez nous ce matin.} What did Hugo do?

options.text: He dropped by their flat this morning.
He spent the whole morning at their flat.
He forgot about them this morning.

items.situation: Maya wants to see Léa's flat. Tell Léa you will drop by her place tonight.
items.answer: je passe chez toi ce soir
accept: je vais passer chez toi ce soir
ce soir, je passe chez toi

mistakes.answer: je passe à toi ce soir
mistakes.feedback: To drop by someone's place: {passer chez}. {Je passe chez toi}.

mistakes.answer: je passer chez toi ce soir

items.instruction: Noé tells Maya about last Saturday. Put his sentence in the past.
items.shown: Je passe le samedi à la piscine.
items.answer: j'ai passé le samedi à la piscine

mistakes.answer: je suis passé le samedi à la piscine
mistakes.feedback: Spending time takes {avoir}: {j'ai passé le samedi}.

mistakes.answer: j'ai passer le samedi à la piscine

items.situation: Hugo asks Léa: {Tu passes chez moi ce soir, hein ?} Answer as Léa, the way friends talk: yeah, at eight.
accept: ouais, je passe à huit heures
ouais, je passe chez toi à huit heures

mistakes.answer: ouais, je passes à huit heures

items.question: Hugo says: {Ouais, mec, je passe chez toi ce soir.} Who is he talking to?

items.text: Léa : J'ai ___ un truc chez Hugo : le livre que je lis.
items.gloss: Léa: I left something at Hugo's: the book I'm reading.

items.situation: Maman is leaving for work. She asks Noé not to forget to drop by the bakery. What does she say?
items.answer: n'oublie pas de passer à la boulangerie
accept: oublie pas de passer à la boulangerie
noé, n'oublie pas de passer à la boulangerie

mistakes.answer: n'oublies pas de passer à la boulangerie
mistakes.feedback: A command to {tu} drops the -s of an -er verb: {n'oublie pas}.

mistakes.answer: n'oublie pas passer à la boulangerie
mistakes.feedback: Forget to do something: {oublier de}. {N'oublie pas de passer}.

items.situation: Noé says {Au revoir !} and runs out, leaving the building door open. Mme Garnier asks him to close the door, please. What does she say?
items.answer: ferme la porte, s'il te plaît
accept: ferme la porte s'il te plaît

mistakes.answer: fermes la porte, s'il te plaît
mistakes.feedback: A command to {tu} drops the -s of an -er verb: {ferme}.

mistakes.answer: ferme la porte, s'il vous plaît
mistakes.feedback: Noé is nine, so Mme Garnier says {tu} to him: {s'il te plaît}.

items.text: Maya est seule devant la porte rouge. Tout à coup, Léa ___ par là.
items.gloss: Maya is alone at the red front door. All of a sudden, Léa comes by.

items.situation: Léa sees Maya stuck at the door and asks: {Ça va, Maya ?} Answer as Maya, the way friends talk: yeah, I forgot my key.

mistakes.answer: ouais, je suis oublié ma clé

items.text: Maya : Mes parents travaillent ce soir. ___, je peux pas entrer.
items.gloss: Maya: My parents are working tonight. Anyway, I can't get in.

mistakes.feedback: {ouais} says yes. To sum up and get to the point: {bref}.

items.question: Maya says: {J'ai oublié ma clé. Bref, je peux pas entrer.} What does {bref} do here?

options.text: It sums up and gets to the point.

items.instruction: Noé comes down the stairs. Léa tells him what Maya just said. Start with {Maya}.

mistakes.feedback: It is Maya's key now: {sa clé}.
